item.title: JavaScript: Parse CSV Data to JSON Objects
item.description:
“JavaScript: Parse CSV Data to JSON Objects”

Parsing Comma Separated Values (CSV) data into JavaScript objects is a common task in web development, especially when dealing with data import or API responses. CSV files, while simple in structure, can present challenges due to variations in formatting, including quoted fields, escaped characters, and different line endings. This post explores several effective methods for converting CSV strings or files into structured JavaScript objects.

item.title: Parsing Complex CSV Strings in JavaScript: Handling Custom Quotes and Escapes
item.description:
“Parsing Complex CSV Strings in JavaScript: Handling Custom Quotes and Escapes”

Extracting values from Comma Separated Values (CSV) strings presents numerous challenges, especially when the input deviates from strict RFC 4180 standards. Issues arise from mixed quoting mechanisms (single vs. double quotes), escaped characters within fields, and varied whitespace handling. How can we reliably convert such complex CSV data into structured arrays of values in JavaScript?

Several effective strategies exist, ranging from highly tailored regular expressions to iterative micro-parsers.

item.title: .NET CSV Parsing: Best Practices and Code Solutions
item.description:
“.NET CSV Parsing: Best Practices and Code Solutions”

When working with comma-separated values (CSV) files in .NET, efficient and accurate parsing is crucial. CSV formats can vary, especially in how they handle delimiters within fields, quoted text, and escaped characters. This post explores various strategies and libraries to help you navigate these complexities and reliably read CSV data.

Utilizing .NET’s Built-in Capabilities

One approach leverages .NET’s built-in functionalities without external dependencies.
